1.name: Roman law
1.info: Written laws, taxes and surveyors for every province.

1.name: The legions
1.info: Paid soldiers who serve for twenty years.

1.name: Latin letters
1.info: One tongue and one alphabet from end to end of the empire.

2.name: Royal estates
2.info: The king's farms and tolls fill the treasury.

2.name: War bands
2.info: Every lord keeps armed men ready to ride.

2.name: Monastic schools
2.info: Monks copy books and teach the sons of the realm.

3.name: Merchant guilds
3.info: Guilds run the markets and keep the roads busy.

3.name: Knightly orders
3.info: Sworn knights hold the castles and lead the charge.

3.name: Cathedral schools
3.info: Master builders and scholars gather round the new cathedrals.

4.name: Banking houses
4.info: Bankers lend to princes and take their share of every trade.

4.name: Military revolution
4.info: Drill, gunpowder and paid soldiers change how wars are fought.

4.name: Patronage of the arts
4.info: Artists and thinkers come to the court that pays them.

5.name: Agricultural revolution
5.info: New crops and rotations feed more people from the same fields.

5.name: Standing army
5.info: Soldiers in uniform all year, ready to march.

5.name: Encyclopedists
5.info: All that is known, written down in one great work.

6.name: Free trade
6.info: Tolls fall and goods move faster than ever.

6.name: Conscription
6.info: Every young man serves; the barracks never stand empty.

6.name: Engineering schools
6.info: Trained engineers make every workshop run better.

techs.name: Herding
techs.info: Sheep, pigs and cattle kept in pens instead of hunted.

techs.name: Irrigation
techs.info: Ditches carry river water to the fields.

techs.name: The wheel
techs.info: Solid wooden wheels under a cart.

techs.name: Pack animals
techs.info: Donkeys and mules carry loads along the roads.

techs.name: Barter and trade
techs.info: Traders come by with copper, tin and cloth to swap.

techs.name: Kilns
techs.info: Bricks fired hot with charcoal, stronger than sun-dried mud.

techs.name: Writing
techs.info: Scribes mark clay tablets: the realm's knowledge is kept.

techs.name: Bows
techs.info: Bowyers make bows for hunters, scouts and archers.

techs.name: Citadels
techs.info: Stone towers on the hills guard the land around them.

techs.name: Weaving
techs.info: Wool spun and woven on an upright loom.

techs.name: Seafaring
techs.info: Planked ships with a square sail carry goods and men over the sea.

techs.name: Lost-wax casting
techs.info: Wax models in clay moulds: finer bronze, cast faster.

techs.name: Bronze armour
techs.info: Breastplates and greaves hammered out of bronze.

techs.name: Log tracks
techs.info: Split logs laid across soft ground: carts no longer sink in the mud.

techs.name: Weights and measures
techs.info: Stone weights and marked rods: fair trade, and fair dues for the realm.

techs.name: Bronze sickles
techs.info: Curved bronze blades reap the grain twice as fast as flint.

techs.name: Storage pits
techs.info: Grain kept dry in lined pits and jars: stores hold more and less is lost.

techs.name: Wild hives
techs.info: Honey taken from hollow trees, then hives in straw baskets by the orchards.

techs.name: Hot furnaces
techs.info: Turf-covered clamps burn clean charcoal, and clay tuyeres blow the furnaces hot enough to melt copper quickly.

techs.name: Tin prospecting
techs.info: Prospectors follow the streams to the richest tin and copper.

techs.name: The potter's wheel
techs.info: Clay shaped on a turning wheel: pots, moulds and bricks come quicker.

techs.name: Village elders
techs.info: Elders settle quarrels at the gate: families come to stay.

techs.name: Harvest festivals
techs.info: Feasts after the harvest bring the villages together.

techs.name: Herb gathering
techs.info: Wise women know which leaves heal and which harm.

techs.name: The calendar
techs.info: Star-watchers count the days to the sowing and the floods.

techs.name: Counting boards
techs.info: Pebbles in grooved boards: sums for the stores and the dues.

techs.name: War chariots
techs.info: Two horses and a bronze-rimmed car: archers that strike and are gone.

techs.name: Shield wall
techs.info: Bronze-faced shields locked side by side.

techs.name: Iron working
techs.info: Iron, harder and far more common than bronze: iron and coal mines, smelters, toolsmiths, weaponsmiths and the mint. Opens the Roman age. Needs 5 of the 28 Bronze techs first.

techs.name: Roman roads
techs.info: Paved, straight and drained: goods move faster.

techs.name: Roman concrete
techs.info: Lime and volcanic ash set hard even under water.

techs.name: Aqueducts
techs.info: Water brought from the hills to the towns.

techs.name: Drilled legions
techs.info: Daily drill, marching camps and the short sword.

techs.name: The new kingdoms
techs.info: Rome's order is gone; kings, lords and bishops rule the land now and collect its dues. Opens the Early Medieval age. Needs 2 Roman techs first.

techs.name: Rise of the towns
techs.info: Markets grow into chartered towns with walls, guilds and councils. Opens the High Medieval age. Needs 8 Early Medieval techs first.

techs.name: Rebirth of learning
techs.info: Old books are found again and read with new eyes: art, trade and science flower. Opens the Renaissance age. Needs 8 High Medieval techs first.

techs.name: Age of reason
techs.info: Measure, test and write it down: reason is put to work on everything. Opens the Enlightenment age. Needs 7 Renaissance techs first.

techs.name: Dawn of industry
techs.info: Coal, iron and steam: the first factories and the people to work them. Opens the Industrial age. Needs 7 Enlightenment techs first.

techs.name: Iron axes
techs.info: Sharper axes fell trees faster.

techs.name: Coppicing
techs.info: Cutting trees back so they regrow.

techs.name: Fish traps
techs.info: Weirs and baskets catch fish while you wait.

techs.name: Wells and cisterns
techs.info: Deeper wells give more water.

techs.name: Heavy plough
techs.info: Deep ploughing for heavy northern soils.

techs.name: Watermills
techs.info: Water wheels drive mills and saws.

techs.name: Stone masonry
techs.info: Better ways to cut stone.

techs.name: Beekeeping
techs.info: Straw skeps and better hives.

techs.name: Tool care
techs.info: Whetstones and grease: some new workers can use an old tool.

techs.name: Longbows
techs.info: Hunters and soldiers shoot further.

techs.name: Granaries
techs.info: Dry stores keep more of every good.

techs.name: Timber framing
techs.info: Quicker, roomier houses.

techs.name: Herbal lore
techs.info: Healthier people need a little less food.

techs.name: Village markets
techs.info: Weekly markets bring goods and coin.

techs.name: Monasteries
techs.info: Monks keep learning alive and brew beer.

techs.name: Chainmail
techs.info: Interlinked rings protect your soldiers.

techs.name: Ox carts
techs.info: Heavy carts pulled by oxen move goods in bulk.

techs.name: Horse collar
techs.info: Horses pull without choking.

techs.name: Apprenticeship
techs.info: Masters teach the young: workers learn their trade faster.

techs.name: Bellows
techs.info: Hotter fires for every metalworker.

techs.name: Shield walls
techs.info: Defenders stand shoulder to shoulder.

techs.name: Open-field farming
techs.info: Long strips ploughed together.

techs.name: Tithes
techs.info: A tenth for the church and its scholars.

techs.name: Feudalism
techs.info: Lords hold land in return for service.

techs.name: Prospecting
techs.info: Geologists survey a wider area (18 tiles), and 4 can be out at once instead of 2.

techs.name: Charcoal clamps
techs.info: Earth-covered stacks burn slower and give more charcoal.

techs.name: Clay working
techs.info: Puddled clay digs and moulds more easily.

techs.name: Hunting dogs
techs.info: Hounds find and drive the game.

techs.name: Village smithy
techs.info: A hotter forge for every village smith.

techs.name: Militia levy
techs.info: Every man owes a few days of drill a year.

techs.name: Pack mules
techs.info: Sure-footed mules where carts can't go.

techs.name: Wool trade
techs.info: Sheep runs and weavers feed the cloth trade.

techs.name: Salt roads
techs.info: Salt preserves fish through winter.

techs.name: Post windmills
techs.info: Mills that turn to face the wind.

techs.name: Cheesemaking
techs.info: Rennet and cellars for ripening.

techs.name: Bark tanning
techs.info: Oak bark makes better leather faster.

techs.name: Trade fairs
techs.info: Regional fairs need large warehouses.

techs.name: Three-field system
techs.info: A third of the land rests each year.

techs.name: Heavy horses
techs.info: Bred to pull heavy loads.

techs.name: Wool combing
techs.info: Finer yarn, faster weaving.

techs.name: Dyeing
techs.info: Colourful cloth sells and sews faster.

techs.name: Brewers' guild
techs.info: Better malt and cleaner vats.

techs.name: Vintners
techs.info: Monks perfect the vine.

techs.name: Hospices
techs.info: Travellers are cared for, and many stay.

techs.name: Cellars
techs.info: Cool cellars under every store.

techs.name: Stone castles
techs.info: Great stone keeps anchor your borders.

techs.name: Guilds
techs.info: Craft guilds train masters.

techs.name: Cathedral schools
techs.info: Schools beside the great churches.

techs.name: Town charters
techs.info: Towns buy their freedom and pay for it.

techs.name: Stone roads
techs.info: Firm roads in every weather.

techs.name: Journeymen
techs.info: Travelling workers bring new skills.

techs.name: Papermaking
techs.info: Cheap paper replaces parchment.

techs.name: Crossbows
techs.info: Bolts that pierce mail.

techs.name: Masons' guild
techs.info: Master masons share their secrets.

techs.name: Town walls
techs.info: Stone walls around the towns.

techs.name: Smoke curing
techs.info: Salted and smoked meat keeps through the winter.

techs.name: Candle making
techs.info: Beeswax and tallow, dipped by the hundred.

techs.name: Tanners' guild
techs.info: Guild rules keep the pits busy and the hides good.

techs.name: Herbals
techs.info: Written books of plants and their cures.

techs.name: Glassblowing
techs.info: The blowpipe makes glass quicker than casting.

techs.name: Fulling mills
techs.info: Water-driven hammers finish the cloth.

techs.name: Tournaments
techs.info: Knights keep their skills sharp between wars.

techs.name: Treadwheel cranes
techs.info: Men walking in a great wheel lift the stones.

techs.name: Stone bridges
techs.info: No more waiting at the ford.

techs.name: Cartography
techs.info: Better maps, straighter roads.

techs.name: Printing press
techs.info: Books for everyone who can read.

techs.name: Banking
techs.info: Credit and coin flow faster.

techs.name: Lens grinding
techs.info: Spectacles and clear glass.

techs.name: Engraving
techs.info: Finer work on metal.

techs.name: Standard tool patterns
techs.info: Tools made to the same patterns, faster.

techs.name: Double-entry bookkeeping
techs.info: Every coin counted twice.

techs.name: Humanism
techs.info: Learning for its own sake; people want less.

techs.name: New World crops
techs.info: Potatoes and maize feed more people.

techs.name: Mine pumps
techs.info: Deeper mines stay dry.

techs.name: Guild halls
techs.info: Guilds train and reward their members.

techs.name: Vein surveying
techs.info: Miners follow the ore and waste less of it.

techs.name: Joint-stock companies
techs.info: Shared ventures and big warehouses.

techs.name: Gunpowder
techs.info: Cannon and musket change siege warfare.

techs.name: Musketry
techs.info: Firearms on the battlefield.

techs.name: Star forts
techs.info: Angled walls that cannons can't breach.

techs.name: Geological survey
techs.info: A geologist who finds ore maps its whole vein.

techs.name: Distilling
techs.info: The still turns weak brews into strong spirits.

techs.name: Trip hammers
techs.info: A water wheel drives the forge hammer.

techs.name: Milled coinage
techs.info: Machine-struck coins that can't be clipped.

techs.name: Navigators' school
techs.info: Charts, stars and the compass.

techs.name: Hospitals
techs.info: Wards, nurses and physicians under one roof.

techs.name: Clockmaking
techs.info: The town clock sets the hours of work.

techs.name: Field artillery
techs.info: Light guns that march with the army.

techs.name: Crop rotation
techs.info: Clover and turnips restore the soil.

techs.name: Selective breeding
techs.info: Bigger sheep, fatter pigs, more milk.

techs.name: Lubricants
techs.info: Greased wheels and tools last longer.

techs.name: Blast furnace
techs.info: Hotter furnaces double the yield of smelters.

techs.name: Seed drill
techs.info: Seeds sown in neat rows.

techs.name: Inoculation
techs.info: Fewer people fall ill.

techs.name: Flying shuttle
techs.info: One weaver does the work of two.

techs.name: Porcelain
techs.info: Hotter kilns and finer clay.

techs.name: Town planning
techs.info: Straight streets and bigger houses.

techs.name: Scientific method
techs.info: Experiment, measure, publish.

techs.name: Standing army
techs.info: Drilled, paid, permanent soldiers.

techs.name: Canals
techs.info: Barges carry heavy goods cheaply.

techs.name: Coke smelting
techs.info: Coal turned into coke for hotter furnaces.

techs.name: Drill manuals
techs.info: Soldiers trained by the book.

techs.name: The Encyclopedia
techs.info: All knowledge in one work.

techs.name: Bank notes
techs.info: Paper money speeds up trade.

techs.name: Agricultural societies
techs.info: Gentlemen farmers share what works.

techs.name: Sewers
techs.info: Covered drains carry the filth away.

techs.name: Turnpike roads
techs.info: Toll roads, kept smooth by those who use them.

techs.name: Chemistry
techs.info: Kilns, vats and furnaces run by measure, not guesswork.

techs.name: Bayonets
techs.info: Every musket becomes a pike.

techs.name: Insurance
techs.info: Losses shared are losses survived.

techs.name: Royal academies
techs.info: Paid scholars, prizes and a journal.

techs.name: Textile mills
techs.info: Mechanised spinning and weaving.

techs.name: Canning
techs.info: Food that keeps for years.

techs.name: Gas lighting
techs.info: Lit streets and longer evenings.

techs.name: Power loom
techs.info: Looms driven by engines.

techs.name: Iron ships
techs.info: Bigger boats that last.

techs.name: Steel ploughs
techs.info: Ploughs that cut heavy soil.

techs.name: Steam engine
techs.info: Coal-fired power for every workshop.

techs.name: Mass schooling
techs.info: Every child learns to read.

techs.name: Public health
techs.info: Clean water and sewers.

techs.name: Steam pumps
techs.info: Steam drains the deepest mines.

techs.name: Portland cement
techs.info: Strong, cheap building stone.

techs.name: Machine tools
techs.info: Lathes and planers make tools in quantity.

techs.name: Rifling
techs.info: Accurate guns at long range.

techs.name: Telegraph
techs.info: News travels in seconds.

techs.name: Railways
techs.info: Goods move at the speed of steam.

techs.name: Industrial Revolution
techs.info: The age of industry. With research victory on, the first realm to finish this wins the game.

techs.name: Tenements
techs.info: Tall blocks of flats for the factory hands.

techs.name: Steam trawlers
techs.info: Nets dragged by engines, far out at sea.

techs.name: Blasting powder
techs.info: Drill, charge and blast the rock face.

techs.name: Rotary press
techs.info: Newspapers by the thousand every morning.

techs.name: Breech-loaders
techs.info: Load lying down, fire five times a minute.

repeatables.name: Weapon drill
repeatables.info: More practice at the butts and the pell.

repeatables.name: Track upkeep
repeatables.info: Fill the ruts, clear the fallen trees.

repeatables.name: Craft secrets
repeatables.info: Each master passes on a trick or two.

repeatables.name: Muster
repeatables.info: Regular musters keep the levies ready.

repeatables.name: Workshop practice
repeatables.info: Better ways of working, written down.

repeatables.name: Fortification
repeatables.info: Each year the earthworks grow a little.

repeatables.name: Mass production
repeatables.info: Standard parts and the assembly line.

repeatables.name: Statistics
repeatables.info: Numbers for everything, and a clerk to keep them.

repeatables.name: General staff
repeatables.info: War planned on paper before it is fought.
